version.changelog:
- Added scripts/charts.py to enable visualization of expense data.
- Now supports generating and sending SVG charts: pie, bar, and trend line charts.
- Updated documentation with chart commands and chart storage locations.
- All charts can be requested using natural-language commands and are sent directly in chat.

llm.summary: The skill's files, instructions, and data access are consistent with a local bilingual expense-tracking/bookkeeping tool that reads/writes a ledger under the user's home directory; nothing indicates covert network exfiltration or unrelated credential access.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (expense tracking, bilingual reports, exports, charts) matches the included code and files. The scripts implement ledger management, export, and chart generation and the SKILL.md points to the same data path (~/.qclaw/workspace/expense-ledger). No unrelated credentials, cloud APIs, or unusual binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md confines operations to parsing user messages, updating the local ledger, generating local reports/charts, and exporting CSV/JSON files. The scripts read/write only the ledger/config/export/chart files under the declared workspace. There are no instructions to read other system config or to send data to external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only at registry level) and the code files are bundled with the skill. The scripts are plain Python and do not download remote archives or execute code fetched from arbitrary URLs. One minor note: the skill does not declare a python runtime requirement even though the shipped scripts are Python.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no external credentials, and no special config paths beyond its own workspace under the user's home directory. This is proportional for a local ledger/expense tracker.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (normal). The skill can be invoked autonomously by the agent (platform default). Combined with local file write access, autonomous invocation means it could create/modify entries without further prompts; this is expected for an automated assistant but users should be aware that ledger files may be updated automatically when the agent detects spending messages.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: parse expense messages and store reports locally in ~/.qclaw/workspace/expense-ledger, generate SVG charts, and export CSV/JSON. Before installing, consider: (1) the skill includes Python scripts and will read/write files in your home directory — review the code if you want to confirm behavior; (2) no network calls or external credentials are requested, so it doesn't appear to exfiltrate data, but audit if you require strict offline guarantees; (3) the agent may auto-record expenses when triggered by messages — disable autonomous invocation or limit triggers if you prefer manual control; (4) exports use floats (2 decimal places) — be aware of possible rounding/precision limits for financial accounting and back up your ledger regularly.
